insight.title: Why Reacting Faster Actually Slows You Down
insight.subtitle: How a three-second delay protects your best decisions

sections.text: Every app you own is designed to make you react instantly. But as automation handles the "doing," your only leverage is "thinking." The faster you respond, the less you actually contribute to the result.

Speed often hides shallow logic. When you remove the gap between a prompt and your reaction, you aren't deciding; you are simply processing. Real power lies in the deliberate pause that breaks the cycle.
In tomorrow’s economy, being fast is a commodity. Being right is a premium. A five-second delay in a high-stakes email or meeting allows your intuition to catch up with your reflexes.
Try this today: When you receive a digital notification today, count to five before you touch your device.
Intelligence is the distance you create between a stimulus and your response.

news.title: Oil Prices Surge After US Iran Blockade Plan
news.description: Oil prices rise sharply after the US announces a blockade of Iranian ports, raising concerns over supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz and global energy markets.
news.why: You may pay more for fuel and heating at the pump.

news.title: Nifty, Sensex Tumble 2% After Breakdown Of US
news.description: Indian stock markets tumbled on April 13 after US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad over the weekend broke down. US President Donald Trump has announced a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, leading to surge in oil prices and slump across global markets
news.why: Your retirement savings or personal investments may see lower short-term returns.

news.title: Already under financial pressure, Midwest soybean farmers are squeezed further by tariffs, Iran war
news.description: Midwest soybean farmers are facing an array of compounding issues. Costs, such as equipment, have crept up over time while soybean prices have stayed low. Tariffs levied by the Trump administration last year and the resulting monthslong trade war with China in 2025 only made things worse, they say.
news.why: Prices for items like cooking oil and bread could rise at your grocery store.

news.title: India begins count of its 1.4 billion people
news.description: India is about to conduct the world’s largest census of its predicted 1.4 billion population after a five year COVID-initiated delay, budgeted for almost two billion Australian dollars.More than 3 million paid surveyors, including school teachers and government officials, will head out and knock on each door in India’s hundreds of thousands villages and cities, as the task unfolds with questions around process, data security and the government claim that caste will be included for the first time since the 1930s.
news.why: Local services and infrastructure plans may change to match updated population data.

news.title: SoftBank, NEC, Sony, Honda Form New Company To Target Domestic AI Rollout, Close Gap with US And China
news.description: Japan's top firms, including SoftBank, NEC, Sony and Honda, have formed a new company to develop large-scale artificial intelligence for domestic businesses, aiming to close the gap with U.S. and Chinese rivals. Backed by potential government funding, the venture plans to initially deploy AI models within Japan before expanding into areas like factory robotics. The company is expected to hire around 100 AI engineers and will seek support from a 1 trillion yen government-backed fund.
news.why: You could soon access more advanced AI tools developed specifically for your region.

news.title: Spanish premier urges China to take bigger role in multipolar order
news.description: Pedro Sanchez also called China's trade imbalance with the European Union "unsustainable" and called on Beijing to open its market to European imports.
news.why: Future import costs for electronics and clothing from China may shift for you.

news.title: Taiwan government should lead engagement with China on new measures, senior official says
news.description: TAIPEI: Taiwan's engagement with China on looser controls proposed by Beijing for trade and tourism should be led by the government rather than private party-to-party contacts, a senior Taiwanese security official said on Monday (Apr 13).China on Sunday
news.why: Your travel plans to the region may become easier with new tourism rules.

news.title: How Colonial-Era Extraction Fuels a New Wave of Medical Migration
news.description: Africa faces a critical health worker shortage as rich nations recruit its doctors and nurses. This article explains how colonial-era power structures still shape global health labour flows, why “brain drain” is an incomplete story, and what systemic, reparative reforms are needed for a fairer global health system.
news.why: You might face longer wait times for specialized medical care in your city.

news.title: Oil prices resume their climb, Asian markets decline as US prepares for blockade of Hormuz
news.description: Oil prices rise amid US plans for a Hormuz blockade, causing declines in Asian markets and heightened global trading tensions.
news.why: Shipping delays for your overseas online orders could become more frequent.
